articleTitle: Effect of high k dielectric layer on the performance of Silicon based Nanoscale MOSFET
abstract: In this paper, the effect of High K dielectric layer on Silicon based Metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) was studied. As we know MOSFET place a very important role in modern electronics, this work investigates the relationship between drain current and gate voltage in MOSFETs with different High K dielectric materials. The dielectric layer in MOSFETs separates the gate electrode from the semiconductor channel, controlling the flow of current through the device. Silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has historically been the dielectric of choice due to its excellent insulating properties and compatibility with silicon technology. However, as transistor dimensions shrink and performance demands increase, alternative dielectrics with higher permittivity (high-k dielectrics) have gained more prominence. Consequently, MOSFETs employing high-k dielectrics exhibit enhanced performance characteristics, including lower threshold voltages and higher drain currents at equivalent gate voltages compared to SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> based MOSFETs. To understand the dielectric properties of different High-k materials, gate voltage, and drain current is essential for optimizing the MOSFET performance. In this work Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, HfSiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> which has high dielectric constant than SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were used to study the MOSFET performance. The HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> dielectric layer shows more current then the remaining dielectric layers.

articleTitle: Energy Trading Interface for Grid-Tied Wind-Solar Power Generation System
abstract: Surging clean energy demand clashes with grid stability concerns, calling for creative solutions. This work explores the synergy between peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading and grid-connected wind-solar systems. It is apparent that, in the contemporary grid scenario, renewable power injection involving integrated wind-solar power generation is proliferating, and hence grid stability and excess energy utilization become critical challenges. P2P trading emerges as a promising remedy, allowing prosumers (consumers who also produce) to directly exchange surplus energy, fostering a more decentralized and efficient energy system. Leveraging MATLAB simulations, the project assesses the technical feasibility of such systems. It then designs and implements a P2P energy transfer system with a user-friendly dashboard, empowering prosumers to actively participate and optimize their energy usage. By analyzing benefits for both prosumers and the grid, the project showcases the significant potential of P2P trading in paving the way for a sustainable and equitable energy future.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Oral Cancer Detection through Speech Analysis
abstract: Oral Cancer detection remains a vital concern worldwide, with timely diagnosis being key to effective treatment. It utilizes Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) and a novel combination of MFCCs with Short-Time Fourier Transforms (STFTs) to analyze oral audio data. The research highlights the potential of these methods in accurately identifying cancerous conditions. Future directions include integrating advanced machine learning algorithms, enlarging the dataset with diverse cases, and exploring real-time analysis for broader applications. A significant aspect of future work involves implementing this model on portable hardware, such as a Raspberry Pi, to enhance accessibility and practicality in clinical settings, aiming to advance non-invasive diagnostics for early oral cancer detection.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Approach for Plant Disease Detection Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs): A case study in Nagaland
abstract: In the northeastern region of India, Nagaland stands as a significant agricultural hub, where traditional cultivation methods have long been the cornerstone of farming practices. However, with the increasing challenges posed by plant diseases, particularly in crops such as tomato, banana, and rice, there is a pressing need to integrate modern technologies for effective disease detection and management. This paper explores the utilization of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with remote sensing technology as a novel approach to enhance crop health monitoring in Nagaland. Despite prevailing reliance on traditional farming techniques, the adoption of UAV-based remote sensing presents a promising avenue to mitigate the impact of plant diseases. By leveraging high-resolution imagery captured by UAVs, coupled with advanced data analytics techniques, this research aims to develop a robust framework for the early detection of diseases affecting tomato, banana, and rice crops. The proposed methodology includes data acquisition using UAVs, feature extraction from remote sensing data, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) based disease classification, and geospatial mapping of disease prevalence. This research shows promising results with training accuracy of 92.56% and validation accuracy of 95.13%.

articleTitle: Exploring Variational Autoencoders and Generative Latent Time-Series Models for Synthetic Data Generation and Forecasting
abstract: This study examines the fundamental theory necessary for comprehending Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and generative latent time-series models. We will also explain how these models extend the principles of VAEs to the domain of time-series data by incorporating temporal dependencies into the latent space. By leveraging the probabilistic nature of VAEs and the temporal dependencies captured by generative latent time-series models—researchers and practitioners can generate synthetic data for various applications, ranging from image generation to time-series forecasting. Through experiments and examples, we showcase the efficacy of these models in generating synthetic data that closely resembles the characteristics of the original dataset.

articleTitle: Detecting COVID-19 Infection Using Customized Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has affected 775 million people globally, with an estimated death toll of 7 million. Detection methods like reverse transcription polymer chain reaction (RT-PCR) face multiple challenges, including false positive cases, time-consuming, and high cost. A rapid, precise, affordable screening alternative is essential to expedite COVID-19 detection. Various efforts have focused on expediting COVID-19 detection due to the high costs and logistical challenges associated with traditional methods. This paper proposes a customized deep-learning framework architecture for automatically identifying COVID-19 infection in chest X-ray (CXR) images. Multiple neural networks extract deep features from the CXR images, including popular models such as VGG19, DenseNet201, EfficientNet, MobileNetV2, and InceptionV3. The proposed model undergoes training and testing using the QaTa-COVID-19 dataset. The proposed model achieves classification accuracy of 97.06%, with precision, recall, and F1 score rates for COVID-19 cases recorded at 97.34%, 96.36%, and 97.01%, respectively, for the 4-class cases (COVID vs. Normal vs. Pediatric Bacterial Pneumonia vs. Pediatric Viral Pneumonia).

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fault Detection Techniques in Power System
abstract: Fault detection is crucial in power systems to ensure the timely isolation of faulty sections and the maintenance of system stability. In this work, the importance of fault classi- fication and identification in analyzing transmission line faults is emphasized. Three methods for fault detection are proposed and compared: Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), Symmetrical Components (SC), and Wavelet Transform (WT). Current is considered a predominant parameter for detecting faults in the power system network. The three methods are applied and compared based on their ability to differentiate between healthy and faulty sections of the circuit breaker and relay. Results indicate that the WT method is the most suitable, outperforming THD and SC. The comparative analysis reveals that WT is more effective in differentiating the type of faults based on various coefficients. The findings of this study can be utilized to set various parameters in power system simulations in MATLAB, enhancing the efficiency of fault detection mechanisms. The simulation is conducted in MATLAB-Simulink, which generates fault signals for analysis.

articleTitle: Filter Based Saturated Controller for a class of nonlinear Singularly Perturbed System
abstract: The design and implementation of a filter-saturated controller for a singularly perturbed system (SPS), especially implemented in a single-link manipulator (SLM) system, is presented in this study. Singularly perturbed systems exhibit both fast and slow dynamics, which enables the decomposition of the total system into distinct timescales. These systems frequently exhibit complexity and unpredictable behaviour, which may have a negative impact on the performance. These challenges are addressed by designing a nonlinear saturated controller with a filter and disturbance observer using the singular perturbation technique. The controller’s effectiveness is demonstrated by its capability to control the manipulator’s movement efficiently while also effectively handling saturation limits and disturbances. This demonstration underscores the controller’s suitability for real-world applications involving singular perturbations.

articleTitle: Robust Serial Driver Verification Through UVM Framework
abstract: The goal of this work is to provide thorough verification using the Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) to guarantee the accuracy and reliability of serial drivers in contemporary electronic systems. The primary aim is to create a Monitor Module in the UVM framework for the purpose of observing and verifying the behavior of the serial driver in testing and simulation scenarios. The Monitor Module is critical for determining compliance with UVM's standards and improves modularity and reusability. In order to test serial drivers, the project will create a UVM-based verification environment, create a monitor module to track important behaviors of the driver, run a number of test cases to assess functionality and dependability, and expand verification coverage to investigate the communication protocol in detail. In digital electronics, serial driver verification is essential for maintaining system accuracy and robustness. To make protocol compliance evaluation easier, the recommended Serial Driver Verification Scoreboard Module is a great help. Error detection, thorough protocol verification, and efficient reporting are some of its benefits.

articleTitle: Enhanced Crop Protection: Mobile-Net V2 for Pest Identification
abstract: This project introduces a novel crop pest classification system that harnesses the MobileNet architecture, a lightweight convolutional neural network meticulously designed for efficient inference on mobile and embedded devices. Through the utilization of deep learning techniques, our meticulously crafted model achieves an outstanding accuracy rate of 96.89% in accurately identifying and categorizing various types of crop pests, showcasing its formidable potential to revolutionize pest detection within agricultural contexts. The inherent efficiency of the MobileNet architecture renders it particularly well-suited for deployment on platforms with limited computational resources, ensuring scalability and widespread accessibility for farmers operating across diverse agricultural landscapes. Our rigorous experimentation and comprehensive evaluation further validate the robustness and efficacy of our approach, underscoring its practical utility in real-world scenarios. By simplifying and expediting the process of pest identification, our proposed system not only equips farmers with invaluable insights but also empowers them to make informed decisions promptly, thereby facilitating early interventions and enhancing overall pest management practices. This transformative technology holds promise for fostering more sustainable crop production methodologies and ultimately contributing to improved yields and global food security. In conclusion, our project represents a significant leap forward in agricultural technology, offering a cost-effective and scalable solution to the perennial challenge of pest management, while simultaneously paving the way for more resilient and sustainable agricultural systems in the future.

articleTitle: A Wood Anomaly Detection System Based on Electrical Resistivity Tomography and Tiny Machine Learning
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the detection of internal voids or decay anomalies in wood using Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT) and Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML). It proposes an anomaly detection method suitable for large-scale target detection, aiming to achieve multi-tree detection and automated detection of targets. The ERT tree detection model is simulated using COMSOL and MATLAB software. Based on the obtained boundary voltage data, a machine learning model is generated using NanoEdge AI Studio to simulate the detection of internal anomalies in trees. Finally, control circuits and control programs are designed, and the machine learning model is deployed on STM32G4 series microcontrollers. In the simulation detection using NanoEdge AI, 15 sets of anomalies are detected out of 16 sets of data for the multi-cavity model. The tree anomaly detection method based on Electrical Resistivity Tomography and Tiny Machine Learning can effectively detect anomalies in trees. TinyML conserves embedded system resources during multi-target detection, enabling low power consumption and real-time processing.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Slotted Monopole Antenna for C-band and RFID Applications
abstract: A wideband monopole element consisting of a rectangular radiator at the upper side and an imperfect ground plane at the lower side of the substrate is presented in this paper. Antenna’s radiator consists of semicircular and rectangle-shaped slots fed by tapered microstrip line-feeding. The slots help in achieving a wide bandwidth of the suggested work. The design is linearly polarized with a volume of 0:341 0:238 0:02 ( is the lowest resonating wavelength) with a peak gain of 2.25 dBi at 7.92 GHz. The analytical model and comparison with recent literature make it a suitable structure for C-band applications. The proposed work can also be used in as a short-range RFID reader at the 5.8 GHz ISM band.

articleTitle: Integrated Deep Learning and Optimization Strategies for Accurate Cinnamon Bark Disease Classification
abstract: Plant disease identification is crucial for agricultural productivity, especially in crops like cinnamon, which is globally valued for its economic and culinary importance. Diseases can severely affect cinnamon plants, leading to decreased yield and quality. This research aims to automate disease diagnosis and classification in cinnamon plants using deep learning techniques to ensure sustainable cultivation and safeguard this valuable commodity. Multiple deep learning algorithms were applied to a dataset specific to cinnamon species, including ResNet101, GoogleNet, DenseNet, VGG16, and VGG19. Data augmentation techniques were employed to enhance model performance, which resulted in improved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. We proposed Optimized Convolutional Neural Network (OCNN) architectures to further optimize model performance, integrating Elephant Herding Optimization (EHO) with selected CNN architectures. This approach minimizes computation overhead while increasing accuracy by tuning hyperparameters like learning rate, number of epochs, and batch size, enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of disease classification in the automated diagnostic system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity Through Machine Learning: Differentiating Browsing Patterns to Identify Potential Threats
abstract: Browsing history is a crucial element of an individual’s digital footprint, meticulously documenting online activities such as website visits and search queries. This wealth of data not only reveals personal interests and behaviors but also carries significant implications for privacy and cybersecurity. A developed machine learning model utilizes this data to distinguish between the browsing patterns of legitimate users and potential attackers. This innovative approach has the potential to revolutionize organizational security efforts by enabling proactive identification of suspicious activities. In a controlled testing environment, the model demonstrated impressive performance, achieving an accuracy of 97.2%, with the Extra Trees classifier exhibiting the highest precision at 98.5% and a recall rate of 97.0%. These results underscore the model’s capability to effectively pinpoint potential threats, thereby enhancing cybersecurity measures and reducing the risk of breaches. By analyzing deviations from normal browsing patterns, this technique represents a valuable addition to cybersecurity strategies, aimed at protecting critical infrastructures against increasingly sophisticated threats. This approach, therefore, offers significant potential for improving security protocols by providing a more targeted and efficient means of threat detection and prevention.

articleTitle: Enhanced Weather Prediction with Feature Engineered, Time Series Cross Validated Ridge Regression Model
abstract: A wide range of applications pertaining to the weather, such as forecasting, prediction of extreme events and atmospheric analysis uses time series data to estimate the future values of weather elements. Time series models were extensively used earlier in the scenario which are now being largely substituted with deep learning models. Advanced deep neural architectures are found to deliver better performances than multi-variate time series models in handling high dimensional data with large number of temporal multi-variate predictors. Despite the efficacy, deep neural networks become inappropriate in low data regime weather applications due to the complexity, design issues and overfitting. The primary objective of this work is to produce a light-weight solution using classic machine learning models for enhanced weather prediction. The weather data of Kozhikode district, Kerala, India over a period of twenty-three years is taken for the proposed work with maximum temperature as target variable. Fourteen Regression based machine learning algorithms including ensemble models were used to model the data for choosing the best one. Detailed feature engineering helped the models to exploit the underlying patterns and seasonality. On comparison, feature engineered ridge regression model surpassed other models with the best predictive performance. Growing-window forward-validation ensured the temporal ordering during assessment. Additionally, the proposed ridge regression model was evaluated against time series models- baseline model and Seasonal Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), the proposed model excelled with a reduced Mean Absolute Error (MAE) 1.13 and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) 1.54.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Machine Health Monitoring in Cylinder Block Production Lines through Ignition in Industry 4.0
abstract: This research presents a comprehensive health monitoring system designed for servo-drives in Honing Machines within manufacturing environments. The system focuses on real-time monitoring of temperature, current, and feedback sensors to detect faults like overload, voltage fluctuations, sensor errors, and mechanical wear. By integrating fault detection, predictive maintenance, and user-friendly interfaces, the system aims to ensure optimal performance and longevity of servo-drives, contributing to efficient production and high-quality standards in manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Botnet Detection by including payload information of packets through machine learning
abstract: Botnets are collections of compromised devices manipulated by malicious entities. To safeguard against their varied and constantly evolving threats, it is essential to have sophisticated detection techniques in place. In this work, we investigate the utilization of machine learning methodologies for identifying botnets using CTU-13, a large repository that contains a wide range of botnet examples. By extracting features from the packet payloads and the header data, we are able to distinguish between botnet and harmless network traffic. We utilize a range of supervised machine learning techniques, including a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), to identify botnet behavior. With rigorous evaluation, we see the nuanced performance of various machine learning models. In particular, we find that the naive Bayes classifier is very effective in detecting botnets, while CNN shows remarkable accuracy, especially when it is asked to classify botnet data converted to images. We also explore preprocessing techniques that improve the quality of textual data. This helps to improve feature extraction as well as model performance, emphasizing the importance of proper data preparation for cybersecurity analyses. These insights not only shed light on how effective machine learning can be in detecting botnets but also provide actionable recommendations for improving cyber security strategies.

articleTitle: Simulation investigations of a pixelated metasurface absorber comprising CdTe, InAs, and InSb pixels for terahertz radiation
abstract: A metasurface was designed for significant absorption of normally incident terahertz radiation in the spectral range of 2 to 8 THz. This metasurface comprises metaatoms featuring InSb-patched, InAs – patched, CdTe – patched, and unpatched pixels, strategically arranged on the illuminated face of a gold – backed polyimide substrate. Extensive simulations using commercial software have determined that the proposed metasurface design achieves remarkable maximum absorptance of 0.99, with a minimum absorptance of 0.95, within the frequency bands of 0.30893 – 0.59178 THz. The tuning capabilities of the proposed metasurface are characterized by an average tuning rate of 1.1 THz per Tesla (THzT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) and a substantial dynamic range of 0.882 THz when subjected to a controlling magnetostatic field aligned parallel to the incident electric field. The incorporation of InSb, CdTe, and InAs patches proves vastly superior to using patches of only one of these materials.

articleTitle: BEL-PID controller for Vibration Mitigation
abstract: This paper aims to reduce the vibrations of the building during natural disasters to protect the building from structural damage and avoid loss of human lives by using closed loop Intelligent controller inspired by human brain. Brain emotional learning-based intelligent controller (BELBIC) functions like a closed loop system where system learns by using reward signal, which corrects error signals. In this work BEL controller is used in conjunction with the conventional PID controller. It tries to reduce the vibrations by commanding a magneto rheological damper (MRD) through an appropriate command signal based on structural response. The efficiency of BEL-PID controller is compared with the legacy PID controller. The results established that BEL-PID controller is better than the legacy PID controller.

articleTitle: LETFM: A Robust and Key-Space Enhanced Map for Secure IoT Image Encryption
abstract: Owing to its property of ergodicity, unpredictability, sensitive to initial condition with bounded output, chaos is being widely used in designing secure communication systems. In this direction one dimensional chaotic map (CM) are center of attraction recently as they are easy to implement in hardware. Researchers have been reporting that a cryptographically secure data encryption algorithms can be designed using the CMs. This has resulted in tremendous amount of development in designing specially image encryption algorithms using CMs. But most of the traditional one-dimensional CMs lack robustness and large key space. Both factors are very crucial for designing cryptographically secure image encryption algorithms. Considering this gap an attempt has been made in the presented research work to design a one-dimensional CM which is robust besides this has significant key space. The proposed CM contains traditional logistic map (LM) and recently proposed trigonometric function-based CM as seed map. The resulting map is given term logistic exponent trigonometric function map (LETFM). This map has been analyzed in various performance parameters like Lyapunov exponent (LE), bifurcation diagram, sensitivity to initial condition. The simulation results indicate that the suggested map exhibits superior robustness and a substantial key space in comparison to seed maps.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification of LSTM Model for SoC Estimation against Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainties
abstract: Estimation of State of Charge (SoC) with higher accuracy is very essential for range prediction, optimal discharging of Lithium-ion batteries, etc. Physics-based models are commonly employed for SoC estimation to achieve higher accuracy. However, it is challenging due to the need of precise initial SoC. To address this issue, data-driven approach is used to develop SoC prediction model. The effectiveness of data driven models strongly relies on reliable data and optimal model hyperparameters. The major uncertainties influencing data driven model prediction are aleatoric (data) and epistemic (model). In this paper, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model was developed with optimal hyperparameters using Bayesian algorithm to estimate the SoC of the discharging cycle of Turnigy Graphene Li-Ion Battery with specifications of 5000mAh, 65C for LA92 drive cycle at ambient temperature of 25°C. Further the uncertainty analysis was performed against the developed model with battery data:-voltage, current and temperature against ambient temperature variations and model hyperparameters uncertainties. The results show that the LSTM model predicts the SoC with Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.5033 and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9994. The robust measures such as RMSE, Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD), and Interquartile Range (IQR) were evaluated against aleatoric uncertainties and epistemic uncertainties. These fruitful results of the proposed work help to develop generalized robust model in future for real-time data with variability.

articleTitle: Melanoma Skin Cancer Detection Using InvolutionNet
abstract: Early and precise detection of melanoma skin cancer is very critical in improving outcomes for patients’ well-being. Deep learning techniques, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown remarkable success towards achieving this goal. They are a corner stone in medical image processing. Despite the success, they have some limitations such as high computational complexity, lack of efficient long range dependency modeling, and the need for extensive data augmentation. This study proposes InvolutionNet model for melanoma classification, aiming to address these shortcomings. InvolutionNet incorporates the involution operation which allows the model to have better long-range dependencies and relationships across channels. We introduce an involution-based architecture tailored for melanoma detection. The InvolutionNet model achieves an overall accuracy of 87.0%. The model achieves a weighted F1-score of 0.87. The precision for the benign and malignant class comes out as 0.85 and 0.90 respectively. The recall for the benign and malignant class comes out as 0.91 and 0.83 respectively. These finding demonstrate the potential of InvolutionNet for precise melanoma classification. The model showcases competitive or superior performance compared to existing CNN architectures proposed in the literature. The proposed methodology contributes to the advancement of computer aided melanoma detection and accurate diagnosis. It also promotes the adoption of involution in medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Health Prediction Using HRV Parameters: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of RF Classifier, SVMs, LR and KNN machine learning algorithms for predicting cardiovascular health based on Heart Rate Variability data. Physio-net platform provided a dataset with four HRV features namely Mean RR, SDNN, RMSSD and pNN50 for further assessment. To evaluate the algorithm, precision, accuracy, recall, F1 score were used as metrics. According to the result the RF showed highest accuracy in prediction of heart diseases followed closely by LR, SVM and KNN. This investigation gives important insights into using machine learning for predicting heart disease outcomes through HRV analysis.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Analysis of Micro Needle for Drug Delivery
abstract: MEMS-based micro-needles that are inserted into the derma and body-covering fat layer of human skin by touch. The cross-sectional areas of the needle bores were optimized taking into account the mechanical stress against channel flow and needle deflection. We typically use the longest microneedle possible to complete the skin penetration procedure, allowing the fluid to go to its intended location without causing any discomfort during insertion. The findings of the microneedle simulation were clear, showing that the stresses caused by the applied masses were below the Silicon's yield strength by utilizing COMSOL MULTIPHYSICS v5.5, the mechanical and fluidic models of the microneedles are intended and simulated.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Approach based Multi-Model Cascade Control strategy for Nonlinear Processes
abstract: Nonlinear process modeling and control is a challenging research problem. When compared to the traditional control strategies, Multimodel approach is widely used because of its capability of providing better performance in which based on the operating region, several linear models are attained for the nonlinear process. Furthermore, for each model controllers are designed and from the designated set of local controllers, a global controller is designed. In this paper, better control of multi-model cascade control system for nonlinear processes is obtained using fractional order approach and simulation studies are performed on Conical and Spherical tank processes. The recommended control approach provides improved performance over conventional integer order controllers.

articleTitle: Gut Microbiome based Cardiovascular Prediction using Random Forest Model
abstract: Gut microbiome in human beings is associated with numerous physiological functions including several of those linked with cardiovascular health. In this work, we explore a case study that depicts the ability of gut microbiome data to predict cardiovascular disease (CVD) with the use of a Random Forest machine learning model. With a dataset of 3277 rows of gut microbiome analysis, we developed a model having accuracy of 88.9%. Pivotal predictors in the performance of the model included the expected and predicted species’ abundance ratios, and their possible value can be used as biomarkers for the risk assessment of CVD. The present research demonstrates the power of using gut microbiome data and machine learning methods for this purpose.

articleTitle: Simulink Exploration of Design and Control Techniques for BLDC-Driven Compliant Actuators in the Legged Robotics
abstract: This paper delves into the process of design and control of compliant actuators (CA) powered by Brushless DC (BLDC) motors, utilizing Simulink for analysis. Compliant actuators, which are integral to robotics due to their inherent safety and adaptability, pose a complex optimization challenge due to the interplay between mechanical compliance and electrical drive systems. The research initiates with the creation of a dynamic Simulink model that encapsulates the electromechanical attributes of the compliant actuator system which incorporates conventional six step commutation using hall sensors for BLDC motors. Following this, a systematic investigation of design parameters such as stiffness, damping, and inertia is conducted to enhance actuator performance for specific robotic applications. Furthermore, a variety of control algorithms, including position and speed control using PI controllers are implemented and assessed within the Simulink framework to ensure precise motion control and stability. Through rigorous simulations and comparative studies, research evaluates the influence of different design decisions and control methodologies on crucial performance indicators like response time, accuracy, energy efficiency, and disturbance robustness. The insights derived from this Simulink-based investigation offer valuable direction for the design and deployment of BLDC-driven compliant actuators in real-world robotic systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Process Monitoring Efficiency through Control Limit Adjustment in Multivariate EWMA Charts
abstract: Statistical process control charts have proven to be helpful in process monitoring. The majority of previous research on SPC charts has been on univariate scenarios. This study builds a multivariate exponentially moving average (MEWMA) chart to perform process monitoring in a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR). The normal and faulty data were obtained from the Simulink model of CSTR. Smoothing parameter of EWMA was optimized to maximize process monitoring efficiency. False alarm rate (FAR) and fault detection rate (FDR) were used for calculating the monitoring efficiency. A novel control limit calculation combining T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and square prediction error (SPE) is proposed to increase the accuracy of MEWMA technique.

articleTitle: Investigation of Metasurface Absorber Using CdTe,Graphene and InSb for Terahertz Applications
abstract: This work analyzes the possibilities of graphene, indium antimonide (InSb), and cadmium telluride (CdTe) metasurface absorbers for terahertz (THz) applications. A possible method of regulating THz radiation, which is essential for many applications such as spectroscopy, imaging, and communication systems, is provided by metasurface absorbers. Because of their unique features, CdTe, InSb, and graphene are suitable options for metasurface absorbers in the THz range. High absorption coefficients and tunability are provided by CdTe, large THz absorption is shown by InSb, and ultra-wideband absorption and active modulation are offered by graphene. The results reveal important insights into the performance of the proposed metasurface absorbers in the range of 2-4 THz. The proposed metasurface’s optimum dimensions exhibits dual band effectiveness with absorptance exceeding 91%. The first band ranging between 2.59-2.70 THz displays absorptance 0.91 while the second band ranging between 2.83-2.96 THz shows the absorptance about 0.99 with an average tuning rate of 0.6 THz T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>.

articleTitle: Time-optimal Known Maneuvering Target Interception with Impact Angle in 2D Plane
abstract: In this paper, the maneuvering targets (such as, satellite, missile, aircraft, ships, tanks etc.) interception problem is discussed with any desired impact angles in the two-dimensional (2D) plane by considering the constraints on lateral acceleration, and minimum turn radius. Here, interceptor follows a time-optimal CSC (Circular arc Straight line Circular arc) path for the interception of the target maneuvering in known trajectories with any impact angles. The study encompasses the targets moving in elliptical, infinity-shapes, and parabolic trajectories, each presenting unique challenges in interception scenarios. For each of the trajectories, CSC path for various impact angles is presented. The suggested method discusses standard geometric technique and hence requires less computational time for CSC path generation.

articleTitle: Computational Efficient ER of Wireless Nano Sensor Network under Interference
abstract: The Wireless Nano Sensor Network (WNSN) area is the most important paradigm used in monitoring physical or environmental conditions. However, computational efficiency is the most challenging issue of WNSN. Therefore, this research presents an MGF based computationally efficient approach for WNSN. In particular, this paper presents a novel analytical expression of the Error Rate (ER) of WNSN under interference using MGF based approach. Finally, the impact of different boundaries such as spatial density of nanosensors nodes (λ), SIR of interferers (γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</inf>), SNR of interferers (γ), and path loss exponent (v) are investigated. The results show that for increasing values of SNR, the ER decreases. Whereas, for increasing values of either spatial density of nanosensor nodes or SIR, the ER increases. Moreover, reproduced discoveries show ideal concurrence with the hypothetical foundations. MAPLE 18, which is a computational numerical programming bundle, is utilized in the examination.

articleTitle: Virtual Prototyping of DC-DC Converter in MATLAB and Closed Loop Hardware Implementation using Arduino UNO
abstract: The design, virtual prototyping and hardware implementation of a DC-DC converter targeted for converting 12 V from the lead acid battery to 5 V for feeding all the DC loads in a residential system is discussed in this paper. The increase of residential DC loads, especially at 5 V level, demands efficient power conversion system. The conventional residential distribution system, in the presence of battery for power backup, contains an inverter that converts the 12 V DC into 230 V, 50 Hz AC which is distributed to all the sockets in the residence. For charging or operating the 5 V DC appliances, an AC-DC converter converts the 230 V AC into 5 V DC. It could be clearly seen that two AC-DC conversions take place where a single DC-DC conversion could do the job more efficiently. The apt selection of such a converter for this application is discussed followed by its design. Also, the virtual prototyping for this converter is implemented in MATLAB to mimic the digital controller's function. Another highlight of this paper is owed to the use of Arduino UNO for this purpose which gave rise to promising results when implemented in the hardware.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Sign Language Detection: Bridging Communication Gaps for the Hearing Impaired
abstract: Nowadays people are so busy with their day-to-day work, so people cannot observe the needs and requirements of each other, which results in challenges for people like the deaf and dumb to talk with people. So now, to break the barrier between them, a solution for both gestures and signs mainly focuses on the detection of the sign or image caught on the web camera. The innovative project helps in determining the signs and has various uses which in turn helps people to grab the feelings, emotions, and thoughts of both deaf and dumb people. As a result, another informative tool emerges, offering significantly more efficient utilization. The whole project is about using many advanced features such as Convolution Neural Network (CNN) and Open- Source Computer Vision (Open CV). Each tool which is used plays an effective performance in the project. All the tools are widely accessed all over the world since it is user-friendly and also, they are multi- lingual support. The project undergoes different phases in order of sign detection i.e. when a sign is caught on the camera, the model detects the landmarks, and all the landmarks are connected and separated into frames later on image preprocessing is performed then the labels are detected from the hand, feature extraction helps in detecting labels, the whole process of image preprocessing and feature extraction are performed by CNN, Open CV. The final result of the model is the text of the particular hand gesture displayed. The proposed model gives an accuracy of highest 70.08% using pretrained model and by using CNN model gives an accuracy of 98.02%.

articleTitle: Automated Sentiment Analysis for Instant Feedback on YouTube videos through comments
abstract: YouTube is a popular platform for entertainment, learning, and leisure. With so many content creators on YouTube, the quality of content varies, and creators often get mixed feedback. To know the audience's feedback, the content creator needs to go through numerous comments. Going through huge and plenty of comments manually is a very time-consuming and difficult task for creators. To ease the task of proper and faster audience understanding of the creator’s content, the proposed model involves the development of a model using Natural Language Processing (NLP) for Sentiment Analysis. This model classifies YouTube comments as positive, negative, or neutral sentiments, and is much faster than manually reading. By implementing this approach, content creators can receive a clear report on the audience's reception of their videos. The proposed sentiment model provides a timely analysis of the public's feedback.

articleTitle: An Offline Engineering Analysis Software Platform for Oscillatory Stability Assessment
abstract: This paper introduces an off-line engineering analysis software, "BigSync" used to evaluate oscillatory stability. The software is developed using open source tools, making it more convenient for adaptation. The user will be able to visualize the dominant low-frequency modes extracted from the raw signal, and subsequently, the oscillations can be characterized through instantaneous energy and instantaneous frequency. The user also has access to the mode’s characteristics, such as damping ratio, frequency of oscillation, and energy content. The software will assist system operators and planning engineers in offline oscillation analysis and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Implementation of Plant Model of an Air Vented Dryer system using Data Driven Approach in MATLAB/Simulink
abstract: Now a days, physics-based models are extensively employed across diverse domains to accurately replicate the real-world physics of systems. These systems use mathematical equations and rules derived from physics laws. However, the deployment of physics-based models in simulation environment poses significant challenges because they are high fidelity and computationally complex models. There is a need to leverage these models in control and validation environments to ensure accuracy, stability, and optimal performance. One approach to leverage these models is through the use of Functional Mockup Interface (FMI) standards, which bridges the gap between physical modeling and control system design. But there are also challenges while deploying them in a simulation environment. To address the challenges associated with it, a new approach of data driven modeling using neural network has been studied in this paper. The developed neural network model aims to capture the dynamic behavior of the Air-vented dryer system, enabling smooth integration with MATLAB for Model-In-Loop and Hardware-In-Loop simulation. This approach helps better for simulating high fidelity systems, benefiting various industries which need dynamic system simulations.

articleTitle: ESERS Sensing: Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: Advances in optics and electrochemical technologies enable the development of point-of-use assays for a wide spectrum of analytes including pesticides, toxins, antibiotics, heavy metal ions, and certain harmful microorganisms. These advancements are important for environmental monitoring, and for safeguarding human health. Though the optical and electrochemical sensors offer several advantages individually, the integration of these two technologies helps in achieving lower detection limits with high specificity and provides both electrical and optical properties simultaneously. This article provides insight into the fabrication of a hybrid sensor based on Electrochemical-Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (E-SERS). In this study, the hybrid sensor was employed for the real time detection of the structural changes in the 4-mercaptobenzoic acid (4-MBA) during its electrochemical activity. The study was performed on a screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE). It also discusses on the importance of the electrode modification and its impact on the analysis. The study potentially showed a change in the SERS spectra during the electro-oxidation on the modified SPCE, making it a potential tool in the detection of small molecules.

articleTitle: Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage – A Comparative Study of Traditional Machine Learning Techniques and Mask Generation using CNN
abstract: Intracranial Hemorrhage (ICH) is a life-threatening condition that occurs due to bleeding within the human brain. Medical imaging techniques such as Angiogram, CT angiography, Computed Tomography (CT), Lumbar Puncture, and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), combined with cutting-edge technology, machine learning techniques, and deep learning algorithms have proved to be efficient in the classification and detection of intracranial hemorrhage. This paper provides a comparative study and extensively carries out brain hemorrhage classification using different machine learning models such as kNN, SVM, Decision tree (AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting), Random Forest and Naïve Bayes. The convolutional neural network technique such as AlexNet employed for classification gives better results. Intracranial hemorrhage masking using CNN helps us to perceive the region of hemorrhage using DenseNet-121 and is successful in visualizing the source of bleeding. The open-source Kaggle platform is used for dataset acquisition and comparative study. The results revealed that Gradient Boosting proffers a maximum accuracy of 96.7% whereas the models such as kNN, SVM, Random Forest and Naïve Bayes have achieved an accuracy of 94.5%, 91.8%, 94.3% and 78.8% respectively.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Pitch Motion of Satellite Using Negative-Imaginary Systems Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a robust controller synthesis for the pitch dynamical model of a satellite, employing negative-imaginary systems theory. The control-relevant model of the satellite’s pitch attitude system with negative-imaginary properties is formulated. Subsequently, a controller with strictly negative-imaginary properties is computed to ensure robust stability and notable performance in the presence of uncertainty and external disturbances within the positive feedback control loop. The simulation results presented in the paper demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the robust control method in managing the satellite’s pitch attitude system.

articleTitle: Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection using Support Vector Classifier and Logistic Regression with Principal Component Analysis
abstract: The health of people is seriously threatened by brain tumours, which can have serious repercussions if misdiagnosed or mistreated. Improving results and patient survival rates depend heavily on early identification. In this work, we present a sophisticated method for detecting brain tumours using logistic regression techniques with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Support Vector Classifier (SVC). The Kaggle website provided the dataset for this study, which was preprocessed using a number of techniques, including image scaling. By identifying important traits, PCA was used for feature extraction, which allowed for the accurate diagnosis of brain tumours. The accuracy of two classification methods, SVC and logistic regression, in identifying brain tumours was assessed and contrasted. Our findings show that SVC performs better than logistic regression, with a 98.61% accuracy rate. Additionally, PCA analysis was conducted to reduce the dataset's dimensionality while preserving critical information. The study underscores the importance of employing SVC techniques for precise brain tumor diagnosis and classification, offering researchers and clinicians a reliable tool for formulating effective treatment plans and improving patient care outcomes.

articleTitle: Design and Optimisation of a Telescopic Operational Amplifier
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a telescopic operational amplifier (op-amp) using UMC 180 nm technology for a supply voltage of 1.8 V. A key focus of the design was to achieve a high gain and a wide input common-mode input range (ICMR) to accommodate a broad spectrum of input signals. Significant improvements were implemented on the initial circuit design, enabling the op-amp to attain an impressive DC gain of 70 dB and a unity gain bandwidth of 6.2 MHz. This enhancement underscores its capability to substantially amplify input signals. High gain is essential for amplifying weak signals accurately and for achieving high precision in analog signal processing applications. PVT analysis was conducted as part of the design process to examine parameter variations across different process, voltage, and temperature conditions. The op-amp boasts a functional ICMR between 0.6 V and 1.2 V, making it adaptable to various applications which also signifies a well-balanced design.

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy Through Data Augmentation using Variational Autoencoders in Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of data augmentation on the performance of a simple Deep Neural Network (DNN) architecture, comprising a sequence of fully connected layers interspersed with non-linear activation functions and regularization techniques. The model was trained over 2000 epochs, with and without data augmentation. Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation functions are applied after each layer, except the last, to introduce non-linearity, while dropout regularization is used to enhance model robustness and prevent overfitting. Experimental results reveal that data augmentation significantly enhances model performance. The registered training loss decreased and training accuracy improved significantly with data augmentation technique. The same results are also observed in validation phase. These improvements suggest that data augmentation aids the model in learning more effectively by introducing variability in the training data, enhancing its generalization capability and robustness to variations in unseen datasets.

articleTitle: A framework for Optimizing Resources and Performance Management in Cloudlet Computing Environment
abstract: Mobile computing is a popular approach which enhances the capabilities of mobile devices with the limited resources by utilizing cloud services. However, the effectiveness of mobile computing largely depends on the efficiency of the cloudlet architecture. A new method for creating a highly effective cloudlet which resolves performance concerns in mobile cloud environment has been presented here. The research examines the obstacles appeared by conventional cloudlet architectures, which encompass latency, resource allocation and scalability limitations. The performance measure has been maximized by the proposed cloudlet architecture.

articleTitle: Smart Traffic Control: Leveraging DQN for Improved Urban Mobility
abstract: In urban environments, traffic congestion remains a pervasive challenge, significantly impacting both the economy and quality of life. This issue is addressed in this paper by leveraging Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to optimize traffic signal timings at intersections. The objective is to minimize congestion and enhance overall traffic flow. This involves the creation of a simulation environment modelling real-world traffic scenarios. Within this framework, an RL agent is trained to learn optimal signal timings by iteratively interacting with simulated traffic conditions. This proposed work evaluates the trained model across various scenarios, assessing its adaptability to changing traffic conditions and its effectiveness in minimizing congestion. Results from simulations will demonstrate the potential of RL-based traffic signal optimization in significantly improving traffic flow, reducing congestion-related delays, and enhancing the overall efficiency of urban transportation systems. The findings contribute to the ongoing discourse on intelligent traffic management and underscore the applicability of RL techniques in addressing complex real- world challenges.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dynamic Eccentricity in Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor through Finite Element Method and Machine Learning
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSM) are strong competitors to other motors in commercial and traction applications due to their high efficiency and high speed. As non-uniform air gaps are difficult to identify at the beginning level, over 10% of faults occurring in PMSM are eccentricity-related. This work investigates the effect of dynamic eccentricity in an IPMSM through finite element analysis and a machine learning approach. In this work, an IPMSM of 550 W & 220 V finite element model in ANSYS Maxwell is considered. Eccentric damages ranging from 10% to 40% were included in the model and evaluated for further study. Motor characteristics such as stator current, and radial flux density are compared for both normal and eccentric conditions. Data on motor winding current and air gap flux (radial component) were acquired from the finite element model and faults were examined utilizing MATLAB machine learning tools. The ensemble bagged trees algorithm is employed to analyze the fault which provides an accuracy of 82.5% for stator current.

articleTitle: Enhancing Control Strategy in Switched Reluctance Motors(SRM): A Focus on Event-Triggered Control
abstract: This paper concentrates on the implementation of control techniques, specifically hysteresis control and a novel event-triggered control(ETC), within switched reluctance motor (SRM). The objective of this study is to compare hysteresis control and ETC, particularly focusing on their outcomes, and specifically examining the triggers, which refers to the frequency of communication between the controller and the system. ETC is introduced as a novel approach where control actions are initiated only in response to specific events, such as threshold crossings or significant changes in system variables. Through this method, bandwidth and computational resources are conserved, leading to reduced power consumption and improved efficiency compared to traditional continuous control methods. The selection of control is driven by the nonlinear SRM model and the intrinsic relationship between inductance and current. Given the growing significance of SRM in electric vehicles (EVs) for their potential advantages in efficiency, reliability, and torque density, improving the control mechanism is vital.

articleTitle: Enhancing skin lesion Classification: A machine learning approach using KNN, XGBoost, and Random Forest
abstract: Skin cancer by far is the most prevalent form of cancer in the world. Skin lesions are precursors to the development of skin cancer. Identification of various skin diseases, particularly skin lesions require a high degree of precision. Skin cancer detection efficiency and accuracy can be boosted by Computer aided diagnostic tools. In this paper image-based skin lesion identification method is proposed to classify seven different types of skin cancer. The dataset used here is HAM1000 which contains 10015 images. Basic features were extracted from the dermoscopic images from the dataset. Results acquired from the application of well-known classification models used in the literature show the superiority of the model proposed. The conclusion reached is that KNN achieves higher accuracy than the XGBoost algorithm used in our proposed study. KNN is used because of its quick implementation and highly accurate results. Additionally, the model reaches an accuracy level of 73%. The suggested study aids in the prompt identification of seven types of pigmented skin abnormalities and can be confirmed and addressed in a suitable medical environment.

articleTitle: IoT and Machine Learning based Valve Stiction Estimation in Process Industry
abstract: Stiction in control valves represents an undesirable nonlinear phenomenon. Product quality and process safety frequently suffer due to the occurrence of valve stiction within process control systems utilizing control valves as their final control elements. This paper introduces a straightforward and pragmatic Machine Learning technique, supported by Internet of Things (IoT) technology, for identifying and assessing the initiation of stiction in all pertinent control loops on a periodic basis. Furthermore, this paper suggests an IoT-based innovative approach to facilitate collaboration among industrial experts across multiple process plants, enabling them to explore new avenues for preventive maintenance concerning stiction in control valves.

articleTitle: Real time audio pattern recognition-based door locking system using NI myDAQ
abstract: Door security refers to the measures taken to secure entry points such as doors in a building or property. This can include using locks, deadbolts, keypads, or electronic access control systems to prevent unauthorized access. Door security is crucial for maintaining the safety and privacy of a space, and it can vary in complexity depending on the level of security required for a particular location. The current work focuses on audio pattern-based door locking system. The work integrates main components such as myDAQ and LabVIEW to create a robust and user-friendly door unlocking system. The myDAQ device acts as the hardware interface, capturing and processing signals from the door in response to knocking patterns. LabVIEW, a graphical programming environment, is utilized to design the software interface that interprets these signals. Users can conveniently set and modify their personalized knocking patterns through the LabVIEW interface, enhancing the project’s accessibility. This combination of myDAQ and LabVIEW ensures a seamless integration of hardware and software, making the" Knock Lock" project both efficient and user centric.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized CPW-Fed Multi-Band Antenna for 5G, ISM, and X-Band Applications
abstract: In this paper, a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-Fed dual polarized triple band antenna design has been proposed for applications like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 5G and X-Band Communications. To improve the impedance matching, an octal-shaped slot with tapering sections is made in the ground plane. The suggested antenna achieves circular polarization radiation because it has E-shaped asymmetric stub built into the structure that produce orthogonal degenerate modes. Fractional bandwidth of 46% is achieved for the ISM Band in the frequency range (2.38-3.56 GHz), 12% for the 5G Band in the frequency range (4.91-5.49 GHz) and 16% for the X-Band in the frequency range (7.63-8.91 GHz). Right-Handed Circular Polarization has been achieved for the ISM band while the 5G Bands and X-Bands are Linearly Polarized.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Effect of Imagined Phonemes using EEG Signals
abstract: Understanding the effect of imagining the sound of voice on the human brain can open ways to various applications like speech decoding, helping people with speech disability, brain-computer interaction, and psychological interventions by mentally chanting mantras. There are two publicly available datasets of EEG signals of imagined speech – FEIS and KaraOne. As FEIS uses commercial off-the-shelf mobile EEG device, it has more potential for widespread application. In this study, we use 9 of the 16 phonemes in the FEIS dataset based on the place of articulation of those sounds in the vocal tract – k, t, p, ng, n, m, a, i, and u. In this work, we preprocess the FEIS dataset signals, extract features, and use various machine learning predictors to evaluate the accuracy of classification. Then, we look for the dominant features that drive the classification. We are able to show that there is a spatial correlation between the place of articulation of the sound and the location of the EEG channels which have smaller range of values.

articleTitle: Innovative Expert System for Coronary Heart Disease Diagnosis Utilizing Soft Sets
abstract: In the recent past, there has been a development of a vast array of theories seeking to explain deal with uncertainties. As a branch of artificial intelligence, medical systems supported with mathematical equations have shown great results in disease diagnosis. Soft set theory is a relatively novel field developed by Molodstov that shows a great deal of potential. In this paper, the "Soft Expert System Framework Incorporating Soft Set Theory and Fuzzy Set Theory" is proposed with the aim of providing a new mathematical tool for handling vagueness in diagnosis. We undertook the development of the Soft Expert System (SES) using medical dataset that contains patient records in order to predict coronary artery disease. In this study, the fuzzy set and soft set were utilized to assess the likelihood of the disease based on the variables including age, blood sugar, high density lipoprotein (HDL), low density lipoprotein (LDL), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1C), uric acid, and blood pressure. The methodology includes key procedures: The generic structure includes Data input, Fuzzyfication, Conversion of Fuzzy sets to soft sets, Reduction of parameters in soft sets, Formulation of soft rules and Data output. This system assumes the role of assisting medical practitioners to improve on their diagnostic abilities and will also ensure that the process takes less time as it would in the normal course.

articleTitle: BLDC Motor Speed Control Using Selective Harmonics Elimination (SHE) Inverter
abstract: The design and implementation of a Brushless DC (BLDC) motor specifically tailored for a three-wheeled electric vehicle intended to navigate Indian roads are presented in this paper. The system features a 900W BLDC motor integrated with an inverter incorporating Selective Harmonics Elimination (SHE) and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) techniques. Additionally, it includes a controller with programmable functionality, a buck converter, and a lithium-ion battery system featuring an efficient Battery Management System (BMS). Additionally, it includes a controller with programmable functionality, a buck converter, and a lithium-ion battery system featuring an efficient Battery Management System (BMS). To achieve precise speed control and torque control of the BLDC motor. These methodologies dynamically adjust control signals such as voltage or current based on predictions generated by the model. Consequently, this approach results in smoother motor operation, heightened efficiency, and the ability to adapt to varying operating conditions without relying on explicit rule-based control strategies. A mean squared of 6% is obtained by comparing reference speed with the actual speed , which represents the designed model’s accuracy. Furthermore, the paper assesses the motor’s performance in the MATLAB environment, providing insights into its effectiveness and suitability for real-world applications.

Author Keywords: inverter with a pulse with modulation (PWM)

articleTitle: Counterfeit Currency Detection using Machine Vision and Image Processing
abstract: The widespread use of fake goods and money in international trade presents a serious problem that calls for the creation of sophisticated detection methods and automated solutions. The potential financial losses and security hazards connected with counterfeiting are the driving forces behind this issue's resolution. Despite current detection techniques, they still require improvement in terms of accuracy and efficiency. To improve counterfeit identification, the proposed method makes use of classifiers and a variety of image processing techniques. Possible problems with a false currency identification were included to a customised dataset. The suggested approach shows its efficacy in enhancing detecting skills with an impressive 96% accuracy rate. The results of the study demonstrate how automated image analysis methods can improve counterfeit identification and lay the groundwork for further research in this area.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Cost PLC to Drive Three-Phase Induction Motor using Variable Frequency Drive
abstract: In this paper, we have designed a low-cost indigenous logical control that is not only affordable by micro- and small-scale industries to further the manufacturing and production processes but also to add value to the accuracy and reliability of process automation. A Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) is a specialized computer used for the control and operation of manufacturing processes and machinery. The logical control is designed with two microcontrollers, which are programmed to interface with the Human Machine Interface (HMI) panel and also to communicate with the variable frequency drive. Here, the analog signal scaling method is used to vary the frequency for induction motor speed control. The range of speed achieved was both step-wise and in a continuous manner. The developed prototype is verified in the laboratory as well as with loading conditions, i.e., lathe and computer numerical control (CNC) machines at 40°C.

articleTitle: Sensors for therapeutic drug monitoring for ciprofloxacin
abstract: Ciprofloxacin is a widely used broad-spectrum antibiotic belonging to the class fluoroquinolones, known for its activity against both gram positive and gram-negative bacteria. Owing to its effectiveness, cost and availability, ciprofloxacin is routinely administered to human and veterinary medicine while 40-50% is excreted in its active form to the environment. Self-administration, empirical diagnosis and inappropriate use of ciprofloxacin has contributed to prevalence of resistance in bacteria making therapeutics and prognosis with this antibiotic challenging. To ensure its most effective use, therapeutic drug monitoring of ciprofloxacin is necessary, especially in critical care. This study employs screen printed carbon electrode and screen-printed gold electrodes to detect ciprofloxacin. The pH values of the solution were optimized to pH 5 for SPCE and pH 6 for SPGE. Further cyclic voltammetry analysis was conducted across various concentrations at the optimized pH values for both the sensors. The sensors could detect ciprofloxacin up to 100μg/mL. Similarly, analysis was conducted using synthetic urine samples, which demonstrated a detection limit of 100μg/mL. Additionally, recovery study was also carried out, demonstrating a RSD less than 10% in all cases, depicting its further use in bed side therapeutic drug monitoring.

articleTitle: Prediction Of Pulmonary Fibrosis Disease
abstract: The progressive and potentially fatal lung illness pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is represented by permanent scarring in a lung tissue. A successful treatment of pulmonary function decline requires early diagnosis and close observation. For people with Pulmonary fibrosis (PF), forced vital capacity (FVC), a measurement of maximal exhaled air volume, is an essential marker of lung function. In order to improve PF diagnosis, this work investigates the viability of using deep learning and machine learning models to predict FVC. A set of three models were developed namely the Long Short Term- Memory (LSTM) network to identify sequential patterns in data from clinical trials, a Huber regression model for reliable management of outliers, and a Support Vector Regression (SVR). For model training and assessment, a dataset of 200 patients was used. In the training set, baseline Computed Tomography (CT) scan and the entire history of FVC measurements are provided and, in the testing, set baseline CT scan and only the initial FVC measurements are used. Each model's effectiveness was compared using three performance metrics- Mean Absolute Error, Mean Squared Error and Root Mean Squared Error. The findings showed that all three of the models had potential for predicting FVC, with the SVR be the most efficient in predicting the FVC values as it has the lowest Mean squared error (MSE) which is 0.029. This work demonstrates the potential of deep learning and machine learning for non-invasive FVC prediction, which may allow for early PF detection and prompt intervention for improved clinical results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Layered Machine Learning Approach to Detect and Mitigate Behavioral Based Intrusions in Wireless Sensor Network
abstract: In today’s dynamic cyber-security world, adjusting to emerging attack techniques necessitates creative ways for threat detection and mitigation. Using the KDD Train dataset, a decision tree-based model first differentiates between normal and unusual actions. Subsequently, employing Random Forest increases anomaly detection accuracy. K-means clustering groups attack types together utilizing a similarity index. A stacked ensemble method includes additional models such as gradient boosting and an extra tree classifier to improve accuracy even further. Detection results are recorded in a CSV file, where suspicious packet transfers trigger blockage, with transfer status has been documented. Performance assessment parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are used to evaluate the model’s effectiveness in detecting anomalies and reducing threats. Validation applies to real-world datasets acquired by Wireshark and the KDD test dataset, affirming the framework’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Enhancing Anomaly Detection in Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Networks Using Classical and Ensemble Learning Approaches
abstract: Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) networks, integral to modern transportation systems, are vulnerable to cyber threats due to integration into smart grids and IoT ecosystems. EVSE network A represents a traditional, centralized EV charging infrastructure, whereas EVSE network B denotes a distributed, decentralized charging network with varying levels of connectivity. This research investigates the security landscape of EVSE networks A and B, focusing on the detection and classification of network attacks. Through meticulous comparative analysis, the research highlights the effectiveness of Ensemble Learning over Classical learning models in improving attack classification precision. This approach enhances the precision of attack detection by leveraging diverse algorithms and data sources to mitigate security risks effectively.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dynamic Eccentricity in Switched Reluctance Motors: A Fusion of Finite Element Analysis and Machine Learning
abstract: Switched reluctance motors (SRM) are widely considered for their reliability and fault-tolerant capability. Dynamic eccentricity fault is one of the major mechanical faults that occur in an SRM which induces electrical imbalances leading to increased losses and reduced performance. This work combines the finite element SRM model with machine learning to investigate dynamic eccentricity faults. A 550 W, 220 V finite element SRM model in ANSYS Maxwell is considered for examination. Eccentric fault severities ranging from 10% to 40% are incorporated in the model and considered for analysis. A comparison of motor parameters involving winding currents and airgap flux is conducted between normal and eccentric SRM. The main contribution of this work is to detect the presence of dynamic eccentricity at the beginning stage which causes a slight asymmetry in the distribution of flux lines in the SRM compared to a healthy SRM. Data on motor current and airgap flux density under both healthy and dynamic eccentric conditions are acquired from the machine model. Subsequently, they are subjected to examination using a machine learning tool in MATLAB, and of all algorithms, the Bagged Ensemble obtained an accuracy of 88.5% based on stator current and 66.3% based on air gap flux density.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Gun Detection in Surveillance System using YOLOv9
abstract: The escalating firearm related crimes including open firing, robbery, suicides, mass shootings, homicides, threatening at gun point, etc. has underscored the growing importance of timely detection of weapons. This paper presents a gun detection system based on YOLOv9, a state-of-the-art object detection model not previously utilized in literature for gun detection applications. We conduct a comparative analysis with its predecessor versions of YOLOv9, namely YOLOv5, YOLOv6, YOLOv7 and YOLOv8 to assess their performance in gun detection. Our experiments, conducted on a Gun Movie database, reveal that YOLOv9 consistently outperforms its predecessors, demonstrating that YOLOv9 has a good generalizability in detecting firearms in real-time. Particularly noteworthy are the precision and recall values achieved by YOLOv9, reaching 99.6% and 99%, respectively, demonstrating its superior efficacy in accurately identifying guns.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Retinal Imaging using Transfer Learning for Pathology Detection
abstract: The critical necessity of early diagnosis of retinal diseases utilising ground-breaking approaches in medical image processing is the primary emphasis of the research. Despite the high volume of around 30 million OCT scans taken annually, the work proves that transfer learning is successful in medicine utilising a dataset of less than 1,000 retinal OCT photos. The dataset has been meticulously assembled utilising a hierarchical grading system that incorporates ophthalmologists, senior retinal specialists, undergraduates, and medical students. The four parts are as follows: DRUSEN, NORMAL, CNV, and DME. A ResNet18 Convolutional Neural Network that has already been trained is utilised in this method. The goal of retinal illness classification is being addressed by fine-tuning the last layer. The study's remarkable 94% accuracy rate shows that transfer learning has great potential as a powerful tool for early and precise detection of retinal disorders. Not only does this work add significantly to medical imaging, but it also provides a comprehensive reference for those just starting out in the field who are interested in using CNNs and TL.

articleTitle: Priority Based Efficient User Scheduling in Quadcopter Assisted 5G Network
abstract: In the days to come the Fifth Generation (5G) communication is expected to replace Long Term Evolution (LTE) technology and provide seamless efficiency in terms of throughput and latency. 5G uses New Radio (NR) standards which makes use of higher frequency bands to achieve enormous data rate. In times of need 5G communication could be assisted by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) during emergency situations such as flood or earthquakes to provide temporary mobile communication service. Due to its ease of maneuverability, UAVs that are equipped with 5G antennas can be made to hover over the geographical areas where mobile communication service is required. But due to the power consideration of UAVs, they can take a payload of limited weight, which makes it to carry a small sized 5G antenna. Because of this it can serve less number of users leaving behind those users who actually need communication the most. And hence there is a need for scheduling prioritized users so that they get the emergency services first. The prioritized users may be the first responders during a disaster or the one who is running a high priority application. A priority based scheduling algorithm which is built on the existing Round Robin MAC scheduler is proposed in this article. More resource blocks (RB) are allotted to prioritized users so that they can send more data with low latency. Simulation is done to calculate throughput and latency which proves that the proposed priority based scheduling gives better performance when compared to the aforementioned existing scheduler.

articleTitle: Navigating Data Imbalances in Credit Risk Management: A One-Sided Selection Approach
abstract: Credit scoring plays a vital role in mitigating the information asymmetry that is pervasive on platforms for peer-to-peer (P2P) lending. A considerable challenge stems from the disparity in loan repayment outcomes: a significant minority of loan applicants defaulting on their loans, while the majority fulfilling their repayment obligations. The presence of imbalance in the dataset has the potential to incorporate bias into predictive model, which could lower its performance. In order to address this issue, data balancing techniques are often employed to enhance the performance of credit scoring models through the generation of datasets that are more balanced. This work constructs a robust credit scoring model capable of precisely assessing the creditworthiness of individuals seeking P2P lending. Four distinct classifiers - Logistic Regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are employed. In doing so, it effectively mitigates the distortions that can result from unbalanced data distributions. This work achieves data balance with One-Sided Selection methodology along with Information gain and Pearson correlation which mainly determine the features to include. The proposed model thus works on both balanced and unbalanced datasets. Experimental results show that the standard metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score achieves upto 90.41%, 89.51%, 90.40%, and 89.96%, respectively.

articleTitle: Battery State of Health Prediction using Hybrid PSO-LSTM Algorithm
abstract: State of Health for a Lithium-ion battery refers to the overall condition and performance capability of a battery when is compared to its initial capability. It is one of the key parameters used to assess the reliability and useful life left out for a battery. SoH is often expressed in terms of percentage, where 100% indicates the initial stage of a battery and efficient performance. The SoH gradually decreases as the battery get charged and discharged simultaneously. The SoH of a battery is a crucial parameter in evaluating its current state and predicting its future performance.
